subject: Triage Health — intermittent streaming drops + client retry amplification
body:
From: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@triagehealth.io>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observed streaming drops and client retries (urgent)

Vanessa —

We're seeing a spike in 5xx/429s for our interactive sessions today. Symptoms: long-running chat sessions (web & mobile) abruptly close after ~90s of inactivity, then our client retries immediately and we get a sharp burst of concurrent reconnects that pushes some requests over quota causing 429s. This started around 08:45 PDT. Attached are a short log sample and timestamps.

Can you confirm whether any config changes or infra work was started that would lower the stream idle window? Our mobile SDK was recently updated but we haven't flipped any server flags. This is impacting care workflows.

—Sara
Head of Product, Triage Health

-----Original Message Follows-----

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@triagehealth.io>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:25:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Observed streaming drops and client retries (urgent)

Hi Sara — thanks for the heads up and the logs. Sorry you're hitting this. I'm escalating now to our on-call engineering and will loop in immediate mitigations.

Quick asks: 1) Can you confirm whether the client retry backoff is exponential or fixed (how long before first retry)? 2) Rough estimate of concurrent live sessions at peak when this started?

I will schedule a short call with eng and CS to triage and share a plan within 60 minutes.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

-----Internal (vanessa -> eng ops)-----

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:28:40 -0700
Subject: URGENT: Triage Health streaming drops -> possible idle timeout + retry storm

Sean / Vivek —

Customer reports streaming sessions drop ~90s idle then clients immediately reconnect en masse producing 5xx/429 surge. Logs attached from customer (logs_excerpt.zip). Initial checks: no config flips on our side in last 24h, but we rolled a small autoscaling patch 2h ago (non-user facing) — needs confirmation.

Priority: high — this is affecting clinical workflows. Please:
- Sean: can you check gateway and LB idle timeout settings and any recent kernel changes that might reduce the stream keepalive window?
- Vivek: can you pull per-route 1m error-rate and concurrency around 08:30–09:30 PDT and confirm if there's correlation with our autoscale event?
- Marissa/Ben: start a temporary mitigation playbook: 1) enable token-level throttling for triage account to smooth spikes, 2) issue targeted advisory to clients to enable jitter/exponential backoff, 3) prepare rollback steps if it's our infra change.

I'll send an update to Sara and set a 30-min call.

—Vanessa

-----Internal reply (Sean)-----

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:42:03 -0700
Subject: Re: URGENT: Triage Health streaming drops -> possible idle timeout + retry storm

Quick triage notes:
- Gateway LB idle timeout is 90s by default for TCP keepalives on that pool, we did not change the value in the last 48h.
- There was a control-plane autoscaler patch at 07:45 PDT that changed connection placement behavior (it was intended to rebalance long-lived streams across nodes). The patch is low-risk but could have caused mid-roll drainage.
- Error profile: upstream 5xx from model backends increased coincident with large reconnect fan-in (logs show a spike of SYN and TLS handshake attempts).

Immediate mitigations I can enact now:
1) Roll forward a small LB setting bump to extend idle to 180s (low-risk, should reduce disconnects for idle clients).
2) Enable short-term circuit breaker on triage routes: cap reconnects per-second per-token and return Retry-After with suggested backoff (we can return 3s).
3) Revert the autoscaler change if we see instability after the LB bump.

I'll coordinate with infra to push LB change and circuit breaker as low-risk fixes.

—Sean
Sr. Reliability Engineer

-----Internal reply (Vivek)-----

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:50:21 -0700
Subject: Re: URGENT: Triage Health streaming drops -> possible idle timeout + retry storm

Data pull (08:20–09:40 PDT):
- Peak concurrent sessions for triage: ~3.8k (normal baseline ~1.2k).
- Error rate (5xx) jumped from 0.3% to 6.1% coincident with reconnection fan-in.
- Autoscaler rollout at 07:45 shows a short window of connection migration; correlated with a small spike in per-node CPU but not memory.

Conclusion: Likely a classic client-side keepalive mismatch amplified by rapid client retries after idle disconnects — our autoscaler rebalance probably exposed partially drained nodes so a subset of reconnects pushed certain backends above their headroom.

Action I recommend: LB idle bump + circuit breaker + customer guidance to add randomized exponential backoff. Also capture TCP/TLS handshake failures for deeper fix.

—Vivek

-----External reply (Vanessa -> Sara / Paul)-----

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@triagehealth.io>, Paul Decker <paul.decker@triagehealth.io>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observed streaming drops and client retries (urgent)

Sara / Paul — thanks again for the report and the logs. Summary and immediate plan:

1) Root cause hypothesis: client idle-timeout (90s) + immediate retry behavior created a reconnect fan-in that coincided with our autoscaler rebalance window. A subset of backends experienced surge and returned 5xx/429.

2) Immediate mitigations we have applied (now):
   - LB/TCP idle timeout increased from 90s to 180s for your tenant pool (reduces idle disconnects).
   - Temporary per-token reconnect rate cap and circuit breaker to smooth reconnect bursts (we will return Retry-After: 3s on throttled attempts).
   - Engineering is collecting handshake failure diagnostics; will follow up if we need a rollback of the autoscaler patch.

3) Short-term ask for you: please push a client SDK update with jittered exponential backoff (first retry at ~500–1000ms randomized, then exponential up to 8s). Ben will provide a recommended patch note you can include in release.

4) Next steps: we booked a 30-min call to go over detailed logs and mitigation timeline — invite attached. Goal: confirm whether the LB change resolves behavior and identify a durable SDK strategy.

We aim to confirm a resolution and post-mortem within 72 hours. Apologies for the disruption — we'll keep this front and center until closed.

—Vanessa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: meeting_invite.ics; logs_excerpt.zip attached (from customer).

-----External reply (Sara)-----

From: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@triagehealth.io>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 10:16:36 -0700
Subject: Re: Observed streaming drops and client retries (urgent)

Thanks — we pushed your meeting invite and will get a quick SDK patch out to mobile by EOD. We'll also add jittered backoff to web. Appreciate the quick response and the LB bump. We will provide session counts and a short reproducible test case on the call.

—Sara

-----Internal follow-up (Vanessa summary)-----

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 03:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call summary: triage — mitigations applied and next actions

Team — thanks for the quick turn. TL;DR: LB idle -> 180s, circuit breaker + Retry-After enabled, customer updating SDK with jittered exponential backoff. Actions:
- Sean: monitor per-route 5xx/429 for the next 24h and be ready to revert autoscaler patch if instability persists.
- Vivek: correlate TLS handshake failure logs and report by Monday EOD.
- Marissa/Ben: prepare customer-facing post-mortem and recommended SDK snippet for backoff behavior.
- Vanessa: coordinate post-mortem and update the customer within 72h.

I'll update the HubSpot deal and flag for leadership awareness if the error-rate doesn't drop below 0.5% in 6h.

—Vanessa
